corpus_evidence.method: For each key, label occurrences in the corpus were measured: how many distinct documents it appears in and how many distinct values it takes. R0.3 (spread) is checked by ndocs>=2 OR being family-defining; R0.4 (discriminative power) by distinct_values>=2. The evidence block is carried on every key.

_note_scoping: Each key's applies_to records under which family/subfamily it is MEANINGFUL; the core block applies to every family. (2026-08-03): this scope is a HINT, NOT A HARD LIMIT. The extractor model receives it in its prompt and uses it to decide which questions to ask; if the model writes a value outside scope, that value IS ACCEPTED -- the DB does not reject. Rationale: applies_to derives from observation and is deliberately narrow, but the corpus refutes that narrowness -- a USB adapter also has logic levels, a PXIe module also has a slot width. Measurement (2026-08-03): the raw text of out-of-scope values was CORRECT. A hard limit would lose those correct values. The boundary does not vanish, it becomes VISIBLE: the v_out_of_scope_value view in specs.db reports them and is read to decide when to widen applies_to.

value_statuses.present: Value is explicitly written in the document.
value_statuses.not_specified: Key applies to this product but the document gives no value.
value_statuses.absent: Document explicitly states the ABSENCE of the feature ('Not terminated', 'Non-isolated'). Never generated by inference.
value_statuses.conflicting: Two documents give different values for the same product (e.g. brochure says 2 kg, user manual says 2100 g). With 772 documents / 250 products and spec tables that repeat per doc_type, this is unavoidable; if it were hidden under 'present' the chatbot would randomly pick one answer. Separate status until a fix exists.
value_statuses.superseded: A newer document (document_nodes.scan.last_modified_time / doc revision) invalidated the value for the same product. Old value is not deleted, it is dropped from retrieval.
value_statuses.not_applicable: Key is NEVER valid for this product's family/subfamily -- the question is not asked of this product. NOT `absent`: applies_to derives from observation and is deliberately narrow, 'I didn't observe it' != 'it doesn't exist'. This status is required because the (model x key) matrix is pre-generated; the bootstrap writer writes it, the fact flow never does.

ruleset_exceptions.exception: a component SELECTED as part of the product's configuration is not BOM
ruleset_exceptions.reason: R3.1 excludes IC component manufacturer / MPN (capacitor, regulator: customers don't ask, doesn't distinguish products). Processor and FPGA differ: customers ask directly ('is there an i7 option?') and it's a CONFIGURATION choice that distinguishes products -- both R0.1 and R0.4 are strong (6 and 3 distinct values). The exception is NARROW: only customer-selectable configuration components, not every IC on the board. Not a closed vocabulary, but a normalized string.

_note_statuses: DECISION (2026-08-03): `conflicting` and `superseded` are no longer PROPOSED, they are ACCEPTED. Conflicts already exist in the corpus ('2 kg (typical)' vs '2100 g') and are unavoidable across 250 products x 772 documents; hiding them under 'present' would let the chatbot randomly pick one answer. schema.sql's av_unique_live_uix index is built around exactly this distinction: one live value + conflicts as an explicit status. `not_applicable` was added for matrix pre-generation.
